headline.claim: a prop-carried parked row transfers to 5 maps where a parking-lane cross-section transfers to 1

runtimeLoop.note: materialize/simulate repairs — needed a trace to diagnose

repairLoop.conclusion: the runtime loop ran 4x more often than the schema loop; all four templates validated clean on the first attempt

defects.title: a stationary actor beside the ego steals the episode min-TTC, and the occlusion metric with it
defects.detail: readPair uses circumscribed radii (hypot(l,w)/2) and is lane-agnostic, so two cars 3.5 m apart laterally clamp gap to 0 and TTC to 0 while closing. revealToConflict is computed for the min-TTC pair only, so it silently disappears.
defects.suggestedFix: a `static: true` actor flag that excludes an actor from pair metrics and adds its OBB to the occluder set

defects.title: arrival() cannot aim at a point off the reference lane
defects.detail: PointRef's pose variant ignores tFrac and laneOffset (only pose.s is read), and prepare() rejects an aim point >12 m from the actor's route. For a lane_offset ego the aim point is one lane width off its own route.

evidence.error: arrival_unsolvable: the arrival point is not on ego's route
evidence.workaround: "ttc": "param.arrivalTtc + 3.6 * lane.widthM / param.pedSpeedKph" lifted acceptance 33/57 -> 44/57 and collisions 8 -> 0

defects.suggestedFix: honour tFrac/laneOffset in pointOf and let the solver project rather than reject

defects.title: after() triggers were unreachable through uniscenarios
defects.detail: each materialized interaction was validated inside a synthetic one-interaction scenario, but the engine resolves after() references at scenario level, so every after() failed with "after() references unknown interaction <id>".
defects.fix: the probe scenario now carries a stub for whatever the trigger names; returns interactions[stubs.length]. 25 lines, labelled in-file, CLI suite green 48/48.
defects.impact: school-dartout went from 0 to 142 accepted cells

defects.title: bus_stop anchor features can never bind on any of the five maps
defects.detail: map-intel anchor-lifts bus stops onto the sidewalk/shoulder lane they stand on; clauses.ts only considers point features whose laneRsl is on the driving reference path. Disjoint by construction.

evidence.crosswalksByContrast: yale 11/12 anchor to driving, so `crossing` features do bind

defects.suggestedFix: accept a point feature whose lane is laterally adjacent to the reference path, not only one on it

defects.title: the reveal-to-conflict lever is the one field that cannot be a parameter
defects.detail: FramePose.tFrac is a plain number, not NumberOrExpr, so an occluder's lateral standoff cannot be swept while pose.s can. The ±1 cap also bounds a frame pose to one lane width, and props[].pose.laneOffset is accepted by the schema and silently ignored by buildOccluders.

defects.title: occlusion is only meaningful on a straight, and nothing says so
defects.detail: on a bend the ego->VRU chord short-cuts across the inside of the curve and misses a kerbside occluder; revealToConflict then reports a long plausible number instead of "this occluder does not occlude". Forces curvatureDegPer10m to be a required clause, which is the campaign's largest cost to map coverage.
defects.suggestedFix: an occluderIneffective flag on the trace when a declared occludes pair never had line of sight blocked

defects.title: a document can validate clean and still fail to materialize
defects.detail: tier-1 resolves after() against the authored document, but the materializer folds `set rules.*` and `route(polyline)` at t<=0 into spawn state and removes them from the timeline. school-dartout holds child-commits at t=0.02 to work around it.

defects.title: --limit above 200 is a hard error, not a clamp (limit_exceeded, exit 1)

occluderGapSweep.note: the obvious tier-1 reveal axis moves the metric by 0.06 s over a 14 m sweep; the real levers are VRU speed and dart geometry
rootCauses: 6.4 m spacing between 4.85 m cars leaves 1.55 m gaps; line of sight flickered through them and the flicker period (~4.3 s at walking pace), not the row position, set the last opening. Spacing tightened to 5.3 m.
on a bend the sight line short-cuts across the inside of the curve and misses the row entirely (the worst site swung 42 deg of heading). curvatureDegPer10m became a required clause.

llmFailureModes: models stopped vehicles as actors — silently yields minTTC 0.000 for the wrong pair and deletes the occlusion metric (D1). The most dangerous thing in the stack today.
trusts the parameter it named — occluderGapM validated, matched, simulated and reported plausible numbers while measuring nothing.
reads a metric without checking metrics.minTTC.pair — three of four templates had cells whose min-TTC pair was not the scenario pair.
confuses "the anchor accepted it" with "the scenario is there" — an unanswerable preferred/cosmetic clause scores 1.0 with weight 0, a free pass, so softening a clause usually deletes it.
puts geometry in the wrong coordinate — tFrac is a fraction of lane width capped at ±1, silently ignored on a prop laneOffset; a PointRef pose keeps only its s.
writes prose in the label field — all 3 schema errors in 840 cells of work.
does not simulate early enough — every finding here came from a trace or a sweep; a 3-draw all-maps batch costs ~10 s and catches all of them.
nextCampaign: fix D1 before authoring anything with roadside vehicles
fix D2 (pointOf honouring tFrac) — returns 21% of multiple-threat cells
richmond-field-station has zero promoted instances in this family and el-camino none for C12; both are curvature/runway walls, a 10 s clip with a closer conflict point would likely unlock both
push more mass into the 0.4-1.5 s reveal band (23% today); levers that work are VRU speed and dart geometry
extend to C5 CPFA/CPTA/CPRA and C7 double-parked-truck / hedge occluders, which reuse this spine wholesale
